newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine tax agency mulling IBM payments freeze.
newsitem.headline: Argentine tax agency mulling IBM payments freeze.

text.p: Argentina's tax collecting agency DGI might freeze payments to a joint venture involving the local unit of IBM in a $425 million deal under court investigation, a DGI source said Wednesday.
"The DGI is considering a possible suspension of payments," the source told Reuters under condition of anonymity.

International Business Machines Co's local unit formed a venture with the local automatic teller machine network Banelco to provide DGI with a computing and ATM system to handle pensions payments in 1994.
A judge is probing alleged "serious irregularities" both in the cost and the awarding by decree of the deal.
The DGI source said the tax body may suspend payments "in case any irregularity is proven."
An IBM/Banelco source just said, "We were informed that the DGI formed a committee to reevaluate the deal."
Other IBM Argentina deals are under separate probes.

Another judge is investigating whether bribes were paid in 1993 to ensure that IBM Argentina won a $250 million deal to install a computer system in state-run Banco Nacion. Eleven people, including former Banco Nacion head Aldo Dadone and IBM Argentina's ex-President Ricardo Martorana and former Vice-President Gustavo Soriani, have been indicted in the case.
Yet another judge is probing why a deal between the company and the province of Mendoza government was awarded by decree instead of by tender.
